newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak premier says referendum foiled, turnout low.
newsitem.headline: Slovak premier says referendum foiled, turnout low.

text.p: Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar on Sunday blamed his opponents for "chaos" in a referendum on NATO membership and said Slovakia had missed an important opportunity to show it wanted to join the alliance.

"The referendum was important to show who was in favour of NATO and who was trying to prevent this. It was possible to reach a decision which would be favourable to the Slovak Republic but this was foiled," Meciar told a news conference, adding turnout in the vote was less than 10 percent.

Two days of voting ended in confusion on Saturday after a separate question on whether the president should be directly elected was struck off the ballot at the last minute. Results have yet to be announced but a referendum requires a turnout of more than 50 percent to be valid.
Meciar said that of those who did vote, some 147,000 had voted for NATO membership and 170,000 against. Slovakia has 3.8 million eligible voters.
Meciar, who opposed amending the way the president is elected, defended Interior Minister Gustav Krajci's decision to remove the question.

"The chaos began when...political parties and the president wrote to the mayors telling them to ignore the government," Meciar said. President Michal Kovac had urged voters not to accept ballot papers without the presidential election question.
